# dependencytrack_service_account (Resource)

Manages a Service Account, a non-human user which authenticates with API Keys or Workload Identity Federation. Permissions and Team memberships are managed with `dependencytrack_user_permission` and `dependencytrack_user_team`, using the `username`. Requires API >= 5.2.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dependencytrack_service_account" "example" {
  name  = "ci-pipeline"
  email = "ci-pipeline@example.com"
}

# Permissions and team memberships are granted with the Service Account username.
resource "dependencytrack_user_permission" "example" {
  username   = dependencytrack_service_account.example.username
  permission = "BOM_UPLOAD"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the Service Account, without the reserved `svc:` prefix. Must start with an alphanumeric character, and contain only alphanumeric characters and `+=,.:@_-`, up to 59 characters. Immutable.

### Optional

- `email` (String) Email address of the Service Account.
- `suspended` (Boolean) Whether the Service Account is suspended. A suspended Service Account cannot authenticate. Defaults to false.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier for the Service Account. Equal to the Name.
- `username` (String) Username of the Service Account, which is the Name with the `svc:` prefix.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import using the Service Account name, without the `svc:` prefix.
terraform import dependencytrack_service_account.example ci-pipeline
```
